evidence.title: Interventions test selected internal-mechanism explanations while exposing instrument limits
evidence.observation: Source-reported finding: Selected language-model case studies connect proposed internal mechanisms to output changes using feature interventions and prompt variations. A backwards-reasoning example was tested by inhibiting features and changing the suggested answer. Observation period and measurement context: Experimental calendar dates not established.
evidence.evidence_standing: Source-reported bounded account; study or measurement; not independently reproduced
evidence.glossary_fit: Illustrative or qualifying; does not validate a definition

source_locations.SRC-136: Methods: validating graph hypotheses and limitations; Biology: planning, faithfulness and interventions; July attention extension

evidence.limitations: Selected successes, incomplete replacement models and possible artifacts. Perturbation discrepancies compound across layers; some local effects follow partly from construction. Primarily Claude 3.5 Haiku. No independent model access or reproduction.
evidence.open_questions: Transfer to other populations, tasks and operating environments remains unestablished. Missing measurement details are not inferred.
evidence.support_assessment: Commons interpretation: Illustrates testing a mechanism hypothesis while separating supportive interventions from remaining uncertainty.
evidence.dispute_status: See source version and dispute qualifications; no systematic clearance claimed.
evidence.verification_status: Not independently verified by the Commons

terms.name: Mechanism hypothesis
terms.definition: A provisional explanation specifying how certain conditions, activities, or relationships could produce an observed or anticipated effect. A useful hypothesis names evidence that could support, qualify, or weaken the explanation.

terms.name: Observability
terms.definition: The capacity to obtain and interpret dependable evidence about states, actions, relationships, and consequences relevant to a specified question. Evidence may come from more than one system or organization.
